name: Tarrenmoor Insulin Affordability Act

components.cap_unit: dollars per 30-day supply of insulin collected from a covered resident
source_sentences: Section 3 of the Act provides: "A pharmacy shall not collect from a covered resident more than $35 for each 30-day supply of insulin."
A covered resident is a resident who is uninsured or enrolled in a plan regulated under the insurance code.
The cap applies to insulin dispensed on prescription and binds every "pharmacy licensed by the Board of Pharmacy under chapter 18".
The Board of Pharmacy enforces the cap: a $1,000 fine for each overcharge, paid into the Fund; repeated violation may lead to suspension of a license or permit.
The Board is funded by license and permit fees; the Act gives it no new money.
The bill was introduced on 15 January 2027 and signed on 12 April 2027. The Act takes effect on 1 January 2028.
Section 4(a) provides that the pharmacy bills the balance to the plan, "which shall pay it on the terms of its pharmacy contract".
Section 4(b) establishes the Insulin Access Fund, run by the Department of Health, for insulin fills of uninsured residents.
The Fund pays the pharmacy "the pharmacy's usual and customary price, less $35, but not more than the wholesale acquisition cost plus 20 percent, less $35".
The usual and customary price is "the price the pharmacy charges a cash-paying customer who is not a covered resident".
The uninsured resident attests at the pharmacy to having no coverage.
Section 6 provides that the Fund is paid "such sums as are necessary" from general revenue; fines under section 7 are paid into the Fund.
The bill was introduced on 15 January 2027 and signed on 12 April 2027. The Act takes effect on 1 January 2028.
The Department of Health runs the Fund through a claims contract (about $3 million a year, paid from the Fund).

unclear.text: Whether out-of-state mail-order pharmacies holding a nonresident permit are bound by section 3 (a pharmacy licensed under chapter 18).
readings: U1-a: a nonresident permit holder is a pharmacy licensed under chapter 18; out-of-state mail-order pharmacies are bound and may bill the plan or the Fund for the balance
U1-b: only in-state licensees are bound; out-of-state pharmacies collect the plan's ordinary cost sharing and cannot bill the Fund

context: Tarrenmoor has about 1,050 pharmacies licensed under chapter 18, section 18-4 (pharmacies located in the state), and about 140 nonresident permit holders under section 18-9.

About 70% of members of state-regulated plans pay more than $35 in a typical month; about 40% of uninsured cash buyers and 15% of high-deductible members said in a 2026 survey that they had used less insulin than prescribed because of cost.
List prices are set nationally by three manufacturers; the 58,000 users the Act reaches are about 0.7% of the national total.
